calls.head: A shadow job for DeBrincat, Finnie and Brandsegg-Nygård
calls.body: At home, the Red Wings keep sending DeBrincat’s line (DeBrincat, Finnie and Brandsegg-Nygård) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Todd McLellan has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Flyers’ first line is Couturier, Tippett and Zegras.

calls.head: Where the Red Wings have the edge: shot volume
calls.body: The Red Wings are around the middle of the league for shot volume, and the Flyers are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Red Wings’ shot volume score is higher than the Flyers’.

DET.head: We leaned Detroit’s way (59%), and they came through.

PHI.head: We had Philadelphia as slight underdogs (41%), and it went Detroit’s way.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Still no win for the Flyers
paras: Matvei Michkov struck first for the Flyers late in the first, but that’s where Philadelphia’s luck ran out. Anton Johansson, in his seventh NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Dylan Larkin, early in the second to tie it 1-1. Andrew Copp put the Red Wings ahead for good with less than five minutes left.

The Red Wings drove the play, outshooting the Flyers 26-18, and the scoreboard caught up. Daniil Tarasov made 17 saves for the Red Wings, and Joseph Woll stopped 24 of 26. The Wings moved to 2-3-2. The Flyers are still looking for their first win of the season, now 0-6-3.

items.text: The Red Wings won for the first time in four games.
Lucas Raymond’s five-game point streak against Philadelphia ended.
Andrew Copp scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 19 (19 games played since).
One of the preview’s two calls held.
